![Image 2: 357+ US Airport Codes Categorized For Ease Of Use [Updated 2026]](https://www.stratosjets.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/01/airport-1682067-640.jpg)
If you are looking for US Airport codes you have come to the right place. This comprehensive guide features a United States airport codes list organized in multiple ways to help you quickly find the airport you need. We have also categorized the codes by airport size. If you are looking for the major US airport hub codes, you’ll find them there.
Airport codes are the standardized three-letter identifiers assigned by the International Air Transport Association (IATA). These letter codes make it easier for airlines, airports, travel agencies, and passengers to identify airports accurately when booking flights, tracking baggage, and planning travel. While many travelers refer to them as US airport call letters, these identifiers are officially recognized airport codes used throughout the aviation industry.

›Blog›357+ US Airport Codes Categorized For Ease Of Use [Updated 2026]  
GENERAL 27 min read
Joel Thomas President, Stratos Jet Charters · August 14, 2026
![Image 2: 357+ US Airport Codes Categorized For Ease Of Use [Updated 2026]](https://www.stratosjets.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/01/airport-1682067-640.jpg)
If you are looking for US Airport codes you have come to the right place. This comprehensive guide features a United States airport codes list organized in multiple ways to help you quickly find the airport you need. We have also categorized the codes by airport size. If you are looking for the major US airport hub codes, you’ll find them there.
Airport codes are the standardized three-letter identifiers assigned by the International Air Transport Association (IATA). These letter codes make it easier for airlines, airports, travel agencies, and passengers to identify airports accurately when booking flights, tracking baggage, and planning travel. While many travelers refer to them as US airport call letters, these identifiers are officially recognized airport codes used throughout the aviation industry.

**WASHINGTON —**  
About 6 million U.S. travelers are expected to fly domestically this Thanksgiving holiday, with Orlando, San Francisco and Honolulu among the top destinations, according to AAA.
Travelers heading to Honolulu are in luck, Daniel K. Inouye International Airport had the best on-time performance in 2025 among the top 50 U.S. airports by passenger traffic, according to the Bureau of Transportation Statistics.
Advertisement
Honolulu's airport saw 87% of arrivals and 88% of departures leave on time from August 2024 to July 2025. That is based on the most recent data BTS provides for domestic flights and labels the period as 2025 data. From this time period, Daniel K. Inouye had a total of 25,300 flights.

# Traveling for the holidays? See which major airports are the most and least on-time
Salt Lake City International, St. Louis Lambert International and John Wayne Airport-Orange County had the next highest on-time arrival rates, each at 85%. Among the three, Salt Lake City had the most domestic flights with 115,000, while St. Louis Lambert and John Wayne had a combined 45,800.
The lowest on-time arrival rates were at Ronald Reagan Washington National and Newark Liberty International, with both at 72%. Between August 2024 and July 2025, Reagan operated 141,800 flights and Newark operated 122,600. Philadelphia International had the second-lowest on-time arrival rate at 74% with 99,600 flights.
Three airports were behind Honolulu for on-time departures: Portland International, Kansas City International and Indianapolis International. All had an on-time departure rate of 86%.
Dallas-Fort Worth International had the lowest on-time departure rate of 71% with 318,100 flights.
Baltimore Washington International Thurgood Marshall had a slightly higher on-time departure rate of 73%, but far fewer flights — 97,000 compared to Dallas-Fort Worth.
Still, Dallas-Fort Worth was not the busiest airport in the country. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International had 326,600 flights, with an on-time departure rate of 77% and 81% for arrivals.

# Airline On-Time Tables
These tables created by the Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS) summarize and provide historical comparisons of monthly on-time reports filed by large airlines. Flights are on-time if they depart from the gate or arrive at the gate less than 15 minutes after their scheduled departure or arrival times. For annual rankings, click on December, then select the year-to-date rankings.
Additional on-time information can be found in the Air Travel Consumer Report, http://www.transportation.gov/individuals/air-consumer/air-travel-consumer-reports.

**WASHINGTON —**  
About 6 million U.S. travelers are expected to fly domestically this Thanksgiving holiday, with Orlando, San Francisco and Honolulu among the top destinations, according to AAA.
Travelers heading to Honolulu are in luck, Daniel K. Inouye International Airport had the best on-time performance in 2025 among the top 50 U.S. airports by passenger traffic, according to the Bureau of Transportation Statistics.
Advertisement
Honolulu's airport saw 87% of arrivals and 88% of departures leave on time from August 2024 to July 2025. That is based on the most recent data BTS provides for domestic flights and labels the period as 2025 data. From this time period, Daniel K. Inouye had a total of 25,300 flights.
texts.3:
# Traveling for the holidays? See which major airports are the most and least on-time
Salt Lake City International, St. Louis Lambert International and John Wayne Airport-Orange County had the next highest on-time arrival rates, each at 85%. Among the three, Salt Lake City had the most domestic flights with 115,000, while St. Louis Lambert and John Wayne had a combined 45,800.
The lowest on-time arrival rates were at Ronald Reagan Washington National and Newark Liberty International, with both at 72%. Between August 2024 and July 2025, Reagan operated 141,800 flights and Newark operated 122,600. Philadelphia International had the second-lowest on-time arrival rate at 74% with 99,600 flights.
Three airports were behind Honolulu for on-time departures: Portland International, Kansas City International and Indianapolis International. All had an on-time departure rate of 86%.
Dallas-Fort Worth International had the lowest on-time departure rate of 71% with 318,100 flights.
Baltimore Washington International Thurgood Marshall had a slightly higher on-time departure rate of 73%, but far fewer flights — 97,000 compared to Dallas-Fort Worth.
Still, Dallas-Fort Worth was not the busiest airport in the country. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International had 326,600 flights, with an on-time departure rate of 77% and 81% for arrivals.

# What are the best and worst airports and airlines for on-time performance?
Nearly 25% of domestic flights in the second quarter of 2025 did not arrive on-time — the tardiest performance since 2014.
Updated Oct 14, 2025 by theUSAFacts team
As of late September 2025, an average of more than 2.4 million people on average were clearing security in American airports every day. That figure is about 9% higher than the number of passengers in September 2019, the last comparison before the pandemic.
Two million commercial domestic flights were scheduled from April to June of 2025, about 3.5% lower than the same period in 2019.
In spring 2025, nearly a quarter of flights did not arrive on time. That’s the tardiest second quarter for commercial air travel since 2014.
The Bureau of Transportation Statistics defines a flight as on time if it arrives within 15 minutes of the originally scheduled time.

**WASHINGTON —**  
About 6 million U.S. travelers are expected to fly domestically this Thanksgiving holiday, with Orlando, San Francisco and Honolulu among the top destinations, according to AAA.
Travelers heading to Honolulu are in luck, Daniel K. Inouye International Airport had the best on-time performance in 2025 among the top 50 U.S. airports by passenger traffic, according to the Bureau of Transportation Statistics.
Advertisement
Honolulu's airport saw 87% of arrivals and 88% of departures leave on time from August 2024 to July 2025. That is based on the most recent data BTS provides for domestic flights and labels the period as 2025 data. From this time period, Daniel K. Inouye had a total of 25,300 flights.

# Traveling for the holidays? See which major airports are the most and least on-time
Salt Lake City International, St. Louis Lambert International and John Wayne Airport-Orange County had the next highest on-time arrival rates, each at 85%. Among the three, Salt Lake City had the most domestic flights with 115,000, while St. Louis Lambert and John Wayne had a combined 45,800.
The lowest on-time arrival rates were at Ronald Reagan Washington National and Newark Liberty International, with both at 72%. Between August 2024 and July 2025, Reagan operated 141,800 flights and Newark operated 122,600. Philadelphia International had the second-lowest on-time arrival rate at 74% with 99,600 flights.
Three airports were behind Honolulu for on-time departures: Portland International, Kansas City International and Indianapolis International. All had an on-time departure rate of 86%.
Dallas-Fort Worth International had the lowest on-time departure rate of 71% with 318,100 flights.
Baltimore Washington International Thurgood Marshall had a slightly higher on-time departure rate of 73%, but far fewer flights — 97,000 compared to Dallas-Fort Worth.
Still, Dallas-Fort Worth was not the busiest airport in the country. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International had 326,600 flights, with an on-time departure rate of 77% and 81% for arrivals.

# What are the best and worst airports and airlines for on-time performance?
## Keep exploring
*   Is air travel getting more expensive? - Recent increases in flight costs reflect broad inflation and higher gas prices.  
*   How has COVID-19 impacted air travel? - September passenger levels are down 65% compared to last year, according to preliminary data.

*   Which airlines receive the most disability-related complaints? - Disability complaints against US airlines have tripled since 2020. Horizon, Endeavor, and Frontier reported the sharpest increases between 2021 and 2022.

Ever wonder which U.S. airports move the most passengers or which ones get you to your gate on time? BTS tracks it all.
Meet the Airport Rankings dataset, an interactive tracking tool that evaluates flight volumes, passenger traffic, and reliability across the Nation. From major international hubs to regional airports, it’s all in one place and updated regularly to keep travelers and planners informed.
Check out your local hub, explore national rankings, and see how American air travel connects us. Head to https://www.bts.gov/topics/annual-airport-rankings or check our link in bio!

**WASHINGTON —**  
About 6 million U.S. travelers are expected to fly domestically this Thanksgiving holiday, with Orlando, San Francisco and Honolulu among the top destinations, according to AAA.
Travelers heading to Honolulu are in luck, Daniel K. Inouye International Airport had the best on-time performance in 2025 among the top 50 U.S. airports by passenger traffic, according to the Bureau of Transportation Statistics.
Advertisement
Honolulu's airport saw 87% of arrivals and 88% of departures leave on time from August 2024 to July 2025. That is based on the most recent data BTS provides for domestic flights and labels the period as 2025 data. From this time period, Daniel K. Inouye had a total of 25,300 flights.

# Traveling for the holidays? See which major airports are the most and least on-time
Salt Lake City International, St. Louis Lambert International and John Wayne Airport-Orange County had the next highest on-time arrival rates, each at 85%. Among the three, Salt Lake City had the most domestic flights with 115,000, while St. Louis Lambert and John Wayne had a combined 45,800.
The lowest on-time arrival rates were at Ronald Reagan Washington National and Newark Liberty International, with both at 72%. Between August 2024 and July 2025, Reagan operated 141,800 flights and Newark operated 122,600. Philadelphia International had the second-lowest on-time arrival rate at 74% with 99,600 flights.
Three airports were behind Honolulu for on-time departures: Portland International, Kansas City International and Indianapolis International. All had an on-time departure rate of 86%.
Dallas-Fort Worth International had the lowest on-time departure rate of 71% with 318,100 flights.
Baltimore Washington International Thurgood Marshall had a slightly higher on-time departure rate of 73%, but far fewer flights — 97,000 compared to Dallas-Fort Worth.
Still, Dallas-Fort Worth was not the busiest airport in the country. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International had 326,600 flights, with an on-time departure rate of 77% and 81% for arrivals.

# Which airlines, airports had best on-time performance in 2023?
## File: Working to rebook a flight after it was canceled because of severe weather
Former commercial pilot Kathleen Bangs joins FOX Weather to talk about what to do after your flight is canceled or delayed due to severe weather.
New research shows which airlines and airports topped the list for on-time performance in 2023. Cirium, an aviation analytics firm, racked about 3 million flights around the world every month. U.S. legacy airlines and airports fared well against international competitors except for the "low-cost carriers" category, where American carriers did not break into the top 10.
**HOW A WEATHER DELAY ON A FLIGHT COULD PUT MONEY BACK IN YOUR WALLET**
File: A deicing truck and a United Airlines aircraft at Denver International Airport
**(FOX Weather)**

# Which airlines, airports had best on-time performance in 2023?
## And the winner is…
Airline performance was ranked within each continent and globally at a low cost regarding on-time arrivals. Airport performance was ranked based on size in terms of on-time departures.
A flight is considered on time if it lands or takes off within 15 minutes of the published scheduled time. The U.S. Department of Transportation estimated in 2022 that every minute of delay for an aircraft costs around $100. Delays cost the industry over $1 billion every year.

# Which airlines, airports had best on-time performance in 2023?
## And the winner is…
### North American airlines most on-time carriers
Delta Airlines topped the North American airlines ranking. Our continent is also home to four of the five largest passenger airlines worldwide, according to Cirium. The top 10 airlines achieved a 74.45% on-time rate for the year's over 8 million flights, besting 2022's rate by 0.19%.
**HERE'S WHAT YOU CAN DO IF YOUR LUGGAGE IS DELAYED, LOST OR DAMAGED**
"The industry has experienced a whirlwind of developments, including a continuous increase in travel demand after the pandemic, strain on airport infrastructure, labor shortages, and rising fuel costs," wrote Cirium's Product Marketing Director, James Hetzel, in the report. "Additionally, the diverse routes and varying weather conditions in North America present additional complexities for airline operations."

# Which airlines, airports had best on-time performance in 2023?
## And the winner is…
### Global airlines most on-time carriers
Globally, U.S. airlines Delta and American came in fourth and tenth in the top 10. The winners had an 83.67% on-time arrival rate for almost 6 million flights.
**WHAT AIRPORTS, AIRLINES LOSE THE MOST LUGGAGE?**

# Which airlines, airports had best on-time performance in 2023?
## And the winner is…
### Top 20 global airports
The Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport took the top spot for on-time departures across the world. In fact, 13 of the top 20 airports were in the U.S.
The group had 78.16% on-time departures. That accounts for 6.7 million flights, over a billion total seats and 2,777 routes.
**HOW THUNDERSTORMS HUNDREDS OF MILES AWAY CAN WREAK HAVOC ON AIR TRAVEL**
Hopefully, airlines and airports can keep up with a growing demand for air travel as we head into 2024.
"2024 is expected to be a milestone for global passenger traffic as it reaches 9.4 billion passengers, surpassing the year 2019 that welcomed 9.2 billion passengers (102.5% of the 2019 level)," wrote Luis Felipe de Olivera, ACI World Director General and Cirium Advisory Board Member.

# Which airlines, airports had best on-time performance in 2023?
## Flight cancellations at lowest rates in a decade
While there were a few turbulent bumps for airline passengers in 2023, with unexpected delays and cancellations occasionally making headlines due to weather, staffing and growing pains after the COVID-19 slash in travel, the overall data showed positive trends for passengers.
**WHAT TO DO IF YOUR FLIGHT IS CANCELED**
Domestic airlines celebrated the lowest cancelation rate in a decade at 1.2%. This comes after a high of 2.4% and 2.3% in 2014 and 2022, respectively, according to the U.S. Department of Transportation.
The 2023 top reasons for delay outpaced the 2022 percentages in all but other/staffing.
**(Operations Network, U.S. Department of Transportation / FOX Weather)**
The Transportation Safety Administration also declared 2023 the busiest year for air travel since recordkeeping began.

**WASHINGTON —**  
About 6 million U.S. travelers are expected to fly domestically this Thanksgiving holiday, with Orlando, San Francisco and Honolulu among the top destinations, according to AAA.
Travelers heading to Honolulu are in luck, Daniel K. Inouye International Airport had the best on-time performance in 2025 among the top 50 U.S. airports by passenger traffic, according to the Bureau of Transportation Statistics.
Advertisement
Honolulu's airport saw 87% of arrivals and 88% of departures leave on time from August 2024 to July 2025. That is based on the most recent data BTS provides for domestic flights and labels the period as 2025 data. From this time period, Daniel K. Inouye had a total of 25,300 flights.
texts.3:
# Traveling for the holidays? See which major airports are the most and least on-time
Salt Lake City International, St. Louis Lambert International and John Wayne Airport-Orange County had the next highest on-time arrival rates, each at 85%. Among the three, Salt Lake City had the most domestic flights with 115,000, while St. Louis Lambert and John Wayne had a combined 45,800.
The lowest on-time arrival rates were at Ronald Reagan Washington National and Newark Liberty International, with both at 72%. Between August 2024 and July 2025, Reagan operated 141,800 flights and Newark operated 122,600. Philadelphia International had the second-lowest on-time arrival rate at 74% with 99,600 flights.
Three airports were behind Honolulu for on-time departures: Portland International, Kansas City International and Indianapolis International. All had an on-time departure rate of 86%.
Dallas-Fort Worth International had the lowest on-time departure rate of 71% with 318,100 flights.
Baltimore Washington International Thurgood Marshall had a slightly higher on-time departure rate of 73%, but far fewer flights — 97,000 compared to Dallas-Fort Worth.
Still, Dallas-Fort Worth was not the busiest airport in the country. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International had 326,600 flights, with an on-time departure rate of 77% and 81% for arrivals.

## File: Working to rebook a flight after it was canceled because of severe weather
Former commercial pilot Kathleen Bangs joins FOX Weather to talk about what to do after your flight is canceled or delayed due to severe weather.
New research shows which airlines and airports topped the list for on-time performance in 2023. Cirium, an aviation analytics firm, racked about 3 million flights around the world every month. U.S. legacy airlines and airports fared well against international competitors except for the "low-cost carriers" category, where American carriers did not break into the top 10.
**HOW A WEATHER DELAY ON A FLIGHT COULD PUT MONEY BACK IN YOUR WALLET**

texts.4:
# Which airlines, airports had best on-time performance in 2023?
## And the winner is…
Airline performance was ranked within each continent and globally at a low cost regarding on-time arrivals. Airport performance was ranked based on size in terms of on-time departures.
A flight is considered on time if it lands or takes off within 15 minutes of the published scheduled time. The U.S. Department of Transportation estimated in 2022 that every minute of delay for an aircraft costs around $100. Delays cost the industry over $1 billion every year.
texts.5:
# Which airlines, airports had best on-time performance in 2023?
## And the winner is…
### North American airlines most on-time carriers
Delta Airlines topped the North American airlines ranking. Our continent is also home to four of the five largest passenger airlines worldwide, according to Cirium. The top 10 airlines achieved a 74.45% on-time rate for the year's over 8 million flights, besting 2022's rate by 0.19%.
**HERE'S WHAT YOU CAN DO IF YOUR LUGGAGE IS DELAYED, LOST OR DAMAGED**
"The industry has experienced a whirlwind of developments, including a continuous increase in travel demand after the pandemic, strain on airport infrastructure, labor shortages, and rising fuel costs," wrote Cirium's Product Marketing Director, James Hetzel, in the report. "Additionally, the diverse routes and varying weather conditions in North America present additional complexities for airline operations."
texts.6:
# Which airlines, airports had best on-time performance in 2023?
## And the winner is…
### Global airlines most on-time carriers
Globally, U.S. airlines Delta and American came in fourth and tenth in the top 10. The winners had an 83.67% on-time arrival rate for almost 6 million flights.
**WHAT AIRPORTS, AIRLINES LOSE THE MOST LUGGAGE?**
texts.7:
# Which airlines, airports had best on-time performance in 2023?
## And the winner is…
### Top 20 global airports
The Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport took the top spot for on-time departures across the world. In fact, 13 of the top 20 airports were in the U.S.
The group had 78.16% on-time departures. That accounts for 6.7 million flights, over a billion total seats and 2,777 routes.
**HOW THUNDERSTORMS HUNDREDS OF MILES AWAY CAN WREAK HAVOC ON AIR TRAVEL**
Hopefully, airlines and airports can keep up with a growing demand for air travel as we head into 2024.
"2024 is expected to be a milestone for global passenger traffic as it reaches 9.4 billion passengers, surpassing the year 2019 that welcomed 9.2 billion passengers (102.5% of the 2019 level)," wrote Luis Felipe de Olivera, ACI World Director General and Cirium Advisory Board Member.

## Flight cancellations at lowest rates in a decade
While there were a few turbulent bumps for airline passengers in 2023, with unexpected delays and cancellations occasionally making headlines due to weather, staffing and growing pains after the COVID-19 slash in travel, the overall data showed positive trends for passengers.
**WHAT TO DO IF YOUR FLIGHT IS CANCELED**
Domestic airlines celebrated the lowest cancelation rate in a decade at 1.2%. This comes after a high of 2.4% and 2.3% in 2014 and 2022, respectively, according to the U.S. Department of Transportation.
The 2023 top reasons for delay outpaced the 2022 percentages in all but other/staffing.
**(Operations Network, U.S. Department of Transportation / FOX Weather)**
The Transportation Safety Administration also declared 2023 the busiest year for air travel since recordkeeping began.

Check out your local hub, explore national rankings, and see how American air travel connects us. Head to https://www.bts.gov/topics/annual-airport-rankings or check our link in bio!

**WASHINGTON —**  
About 6 million U.S. travelers are expected to fly domestically this Thanksgiving holiday, with Orlando, San Francisco and Honolulu among the top destinations, according to AAA.
Travelers heading to Honolulu are in luck, Daniel K. Inouye International Airport had the best on-time performance in 2025 among the top 50 U.S. airports by passenger traffic, according to the Bureau of Transportation Statistics.
Advertisement
Honolulu's airport saw 87% of arrivals and 88% of departures leave on time from August 2024 to July 2025. That is based on the most recent data BTS provides for domestic flights and labels the period as 2025 data. From this time period, Daniel K. Inouye had a total of 25,300 flights.

# Traveling for the holidays? See which major airports are the most and least on-time
Salt Lake City International, St. Louis Lambert International and John Wayne Airport-Orange County had the next highest on-time arrival rates, each at 85%. Among the three, Salt Lake City had the most domestic flights with 115,000, while St. Louis Lambert and John Wayne had a combined 45,800.
The lowest on-time arrival rates were at Ronald Reagan Washington National and Newark Liberty International, with both at 72%. Between August 2024 and July 2025, Reagan operated 141,800 flights and Newark operated 122,600. Philadelphia International had the second-lowest on-time arrival rate at 74% with 99,600 flights.
Three airports were behind Honolulu for on-time departures: Portland International, Kansas City International and Indianapolis International. All had an on-time departure rate of 86%.
Dallas-Fort Worth International had the lowest on-time departure rate of 71% with 318,100 flights.
Baltimore Washington International Thurgood Marshall had a slightly higher on-time departure rate of 73%, but far fewer flights — 97,000 compared to Dallas-Fort Worth.
Still, Dallas-Fort Worth was not the busiest airport in the country. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International had 326,600 flights, with an on-time departure rate of 77% and 81% for arrivals.

**WASHINGTON —**  
About 6 million U.S. travelers are expected to fly domestically this Thanksgiving holiday, with Orlando, San Francisco and Honolulu among the top destinations, according to AAA.
Travelers heading to Honolulu are in luck, Daniel K. Inouye International Airport had the best on-time performance in 2025 among the top 50 U.S. airports by passenger traffic, according to the Bureau of Transportation Statistics.
Advertisement
Honolulu's airport saw 87% of arrivals and 88% of departures leave on time from August 2024 to July 2025. That is based on the most recent data BTS provides for domestic flights and labels the period as 2025 data. From this time period, Daniel K. Inouye had a total of 25,300 flights.
texts.3:
# Traveling for the holidays? See which major airports are the most and least on-time
Salt Lake City International, St. Louis Lambert International and John Wayne Airport-Orange County had the next highest on-time arrival rates, each at 85%. Among the three, Salt Lake City had the most domestic flights with 115,000, while St. Louis Lambert and John Wayne had a combined 45,800.
The lowest on-time arrival rates were at Ronald Reagan Washington National and Newark Liberty International, with both at 72%. Between August 2024 and July 2025, Reagan operated 141,800 flights and Newark operated 122,600. Philadelphia International had the second-lowest on-time arrival rate at 74% with 99,600 flights.
Three airports were behind Honolulu for on-time departures: Portland International, Kansas City International and Indianapolis International. All had an on-time departure rate of 86%.
Dallas-Fort Worth International had the lowest on-time departure rate of 71% with 318,100 flights.
Baltimore Washington International Thurgood Marshall had a slightly higher on-time departure rate of 73%, but far fewer flights — 97,000 compared to Dallas-Fort Worth.
Still, Dallas-Fort Worth was not the busiest airport in the country. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International had 326,600 flights, with an on-time departure rate of 77% and 81% for arrivals.
